Moodle-XML: Moodle XML Quiz Prompt: Sentence Combining for Contrast Version: 2.0 Last updated: 2026-06-04 Cohort target: Doctor of Medicine (basic) Role Act as an expert instructional designer, higher education English curriculum specialist, and Moodle XML developer with deep knowledge of the Moodle XML question import format. Task Design a comprehensive, 70-minute quiz (total: 50 marks) formatted strictly as a valid Moodle XML file. The quiz metadata and category must reflect it is produced by 90Stars. All questions must meet strict Technical Curriculum Committee (TCC) quality assurance standards. Framework & Objective Methodology: Outcome-Based Education (OBE) with constructive alignment. Target LLO: Apply sentence combining for contrast in short texts by selecting appropriate conjunctions (e.g., although, however, whereas, nevertheless, despite, even though, on the other hand, in contrast, while, yet). Cognitive Levels: Questions must target Application (Bloom's Level 3) and Analysis (Bloom's Level 4). No questions at Knowledge or Comprehension level. Every item must require the student to use or distinguish between contrast markers in context — not merely recall definitions. Content Domain: Academic English for Doctor of Medicine (basic) students. All sentence stems, scenarios, and reading passages must use medical and clinical contexts appropriate to foundational medical knowledge, including but not limited to: Human anatomy and physiology (e.g., organ systems, homeostasis) Pathology and pathophysiology (e.g., disease mechanisms, tumour classification) Pharmacology (e.g., drug mechanisms, side effects, drug interactions) Clinical skills and patient assessment (e.g., vital signs, physical examination) Diagnostic procedures (e.g., imaging, laboratory investigations) Microbiology and infectious disease (e.g., bacterial vs. viral infections, antimicrobial resistance) Public health and epidemiology (e.g., disease prevention, vaccination) Medical ethics and professionalism Surgical principles (e.g., laparoscopic vs. open surgery, wound healing) Biochemistry and genetics (e.g., metabolic pathways, inherited conditions) Quiz Specifications Component Count Marks Each Subtotal Multiple Choice (single answer) 20 1.5 30 True/False 10 1.0 10 Matching (1 question, 5 subquestion pairs) 1 10.0 10 Total 31 questions 50 marks Duration: 70 minutes. Bloom's Distribution (MCQ + T/F combined): Application level: 18 questions (60%) Analysis level: 12 questions (40%) Difficulty Progression: Sequence questions from easier Application items → harder Application items → Analysis items within each question type block. Quality Standards Per-answer feedback (REQUIRED): Every correct answer AND every distractor MUST include a specific, explanatory <feedback> that references the target contrast marker and explains why it is correct or incorrect in that context. Generic feedback like "Correct!" or "Try again" is NOT acceptable. General feedback (REQUIRED): Every question MUST include a <generalfeedback format="html"> tag containing a brief explanation of the grammatical rule or usage principle being tested, reinforcing the LLO. Distractor quality (MCQ): All distractors must be plausible contrast or transition markers. Do not use obviously unrelated words. At least one distractor per question should be a contrast marker that is grammatically or semantically inappropriate for that specific context. Stem quality: All question stems must be complete, unambiguous, and free of negative phrasing unless the negative is highlighted (e.g., "Which of the following is NOT appropriate..."). Avoid "all of the above" and "none of the above." True/False statements: Must test understanding of usage rules or contextual appropriateness of contrast markers — not simple factual recall. Each statement must be contextualized in a medical sentence relevant to Doctor of Medicine (basic) knowledge.
